headline: Mysterious Land Changes - Council Says "Not Emergency"

image.alt: A different forest, it was too dark to get a half decent picture

body.text: FISH NEWS EXCLUSIVE: Mysterious forest, hill, lake and waterfall materialise overnight, though the council insists this "does not constitute an emergency."

In news that has left absolutely no cartographer able to sleep soundly, an entire forest, a fully-formed hill, a lake, and a waterfall of apparently magical origin have appeared where, as of yesterday afternoon, there was a car park. Fish News was on the scene within minutes, largely because our reporter had left his 2001 Golf there.

Chunce Whatney, filing personally, was visibly moved. "I have not witnessed growth of this scale, this speed, since the Mayan Empire — right at the very beginning of it, mind you, when the first stones were laid and everyone was still terribly optimistic. I stood in that jungle too. I know what a civilisation smells like when it's just getting started. This smells the same. Damp. Ambitious."

A council spokesperson, speaking from what used to be the car park's payment kiosk and is now the base of a moss-covered boulder, confirmed the land had "undergone some changes" and asked residents to "remain calm and continue to pay for parking via the app, where possible."

body.alt: The forest at night when it was first discovered

body.text: An off-duty ranger, who agreed to comment provided we referred to him only as "a man who works with trees," said the waterfall appeared to be the source of the entire phenomenon. "It's not coming from anywhere. There's no reservoir, no spring, nothing upstream. It's just water, coming out of a hillside that didn't exist on Tuesday. I've stopped asking questions. The pay is the same either way."

A visibly damp hydrologist, called in from two counties over, offered the assessment that the water displayed "properties inconsistent with water," before declining to elaborate further and requesting a lift home.
Local wildlife has reportedly begun moving in already, with several deer spotted looking considerably less confused about the situation than the humans documenting it.
Fish News reached out to the Mayans for comment. They were unavailable, on account of the six centuries.

Chunce Whatney has pledged to monitor the forest, the hill, the lake, and the waterfall personally, "for as long as it takes," which — given the source — he notes could be a very long time indeed, though we believe he may be looking for his car.
